subject: Computer Networks
title: Discover Packet Routing
description: Discover how a packet travels through routers toward its destination.

mission.title: Route a Packet
mission.description: Follow one packet as routers choose a path from Computer A to Server C.

quiz.question: A packet reaches a router. What does the router mainly use to decide where to forward it?

discovery.title: Routers Forward by Destination
discovery.summary: Routers examine destination information and forward packets along a path toward their destination.

sections.title: What is a packet?
sections.content: A packet is a small piece of data sent across a network. Large messages are often split into many packets.

sections.title: What is a router?
sections.content: A router connects networks and forwards packets toward the network where they need to go.

sections.title: Source and destination
sections.content: The source sends the packet. The destination is the device or network the packet is trying to reach.

sections.title: What routing means
sections.content: Routing is the process of choosing a path for a packet through connected networks.

sections.title: Why routers choose paths
sections.content: A router can have more than one outgoing path, so it uses destination information to choose the useful next hop.

sections.title: IP address idea
sections.content: An IP address is a network address that helps identify where a packet should be delivered.

sections.title: Router and end device
sections.content: Computers and servers are end devices that send or receive data. Routers mainly move packets between networks.
